what: Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste runs airports in southeastern Mexico, including Cancun, which is the busiest tourist airport in Latin America, plus airports in Colombia and Puerto Rico.
customers: Airlines paying per passenger, and the passengers spending in the terminals.
money: Cancun, Merida, Cozumel and other southeastern airports
moat: Fifty-year concessions on airports that serve destinations people must fly to, with Cancun channelling the entire Caribbean tourist flow into Mexico.
risks: Cancun traffic depends on American tourism, which follows the United States economy
Mexican tariff reviews every five years set what it may charge
Required capital spending is set by the concession, not by the company
opportunities: 15.2 times earnings with a 28.2% net margin and $968M of cash against $507M of debt
Revenue grew from $919M to $2.0B in four years
Analysts see about 21% upside, and commercial revenue per passenger keeps rising
watch: Passenger traffic at Cancun and commercial revenue per passenger.
